cohort: The study included all singleton births (gestational age >22 weeks <45 weeks) from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway between 1999-2013, totaling 856,300 participants.
finding: Extreme umbilical cord length, entanglement, and cord knot are influenced by maternal and fetal factors, are associated with increased risk of adverse outcomes including perinatal death, and have an increased risk of recurrence in subsequent pregnancies.
mod_finding: A short cord was associated with increased risk of caesarean delivery.
